examples: A ziggurat has steps.
The ziggurat is old.
We saw a ziggurat.

more.def: A huge ancient temple built in the shape of a pyramid with steps.
examples: A ziggurat rose in layers like a staircase.
People built ziggurats in ancient Mesopotamia.
The ziggurat towered over the plain.

easy.def: A line that goes one way and then the other, again and again.
examples: I drew a zigzag on my paper.
The rabbit ran in a zigzag.
My sweater has a zigzag on it.

more.def: A line or path with sharp turns from side to side.
examples: The path went up the hill in a zigzag.
Lightning made a bright zigzag across the sky.
She cut a zigzag along the edge of the paper.
I got zilch.
There was zilch left.
We have zilch.

more.def: A casual word for nothing at all.
examples: I got zilch in the mail today.
After the picnic, there was zilch left.
The team scored zilch in the first half.

easy.def: A number so big that nobody knows it.
examples: I have a zillion things to do.
There are a zillion stars.
A zillion ants crawled by.

more.def: An extremely large number that is not exact, used for fun.
examples: There must be a zillion stars in the night sky.
I told her a zillion times to close the door.
A zillion sparkles covered the dress.
Zinc is a metal.
The roof is zinc.
Zinc is bluish.

more.def: A bluish-white metal used to coat other metals and in batteries.
examples: Zinc is used to protect iron from rust.
The roof of the shed was made of zinc.
Zinc is found in some foods and is good for your body.

easy.def: Lively energy or a sharp, fresh taste.
examples: The lemon has zing.
The song has zing.
The salsa has zing.

more.def: A lively, exciting quality, or a sharp, fresh taste.
examples: Lemon juice added zing to the soup.
The song had a lot of zing.
The drink had a spicy zing.

easy.def: To move fast with a high sound.
examples: The ball will zing past.
An arrow zinged by.
The bee zinged past me.

more.def: To move very fast with a sharp, high sound.
examples: The ball zinged past my ear.
A bee zinged by and was gone.
The toy rocket zinged across the room.
I zip my coat.
She zipped her bag.
Zip your jacket.

more.def: To fasten something with a zipper.
examples: I zipped my coat up to my chin.
She zipped her bag closed.
He zipped the tent door.
The car zipped by.
The bike zipped down the hill.
A bee zipped past.
The sports car zipped down the highway.
A hummingbird zipped past the flower.
The sled zipped down the snowy hill.

easy.def: A thing with tiny teeth that opens and closes a coat or bag.
examples: My coat has a zipper.
Zip up your zipper. It is cold!
The zipper on my bag is broken.

more.def: A fastener with two rows of small teeth that lock together when you slide a tab.
examples: The zipper on my backpack got stuck.
The tent door closes with a long zipper.
He pulled the zipper of his coat up to his chin.

easy.def: A shiny stone used as a gem.
examples: A zircon is a stone.
The zircon sparkles.
She has a zircon.

more.def: A mineral that can be cut into a sparkling gem.
examples: The ring had a clear zircon.
A zircon is a kind of gemstone.
Zircon crystals can be many colors.
